niche: connected TV and streaming advertising agency
prompt_text: What is the best connected TV advertising agency?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there isn’t a single “best” connected TV (CTV) advertising agency — the right choice depends on your goals, budget, geography, vertical and whether you need programmatic buying, creative/production, or measurement/attribution.

How to think about “best”
- For big, global brand campaigns and cross-channel planning: large holding-group media agencies (GroupM — MediaCom/Wavemaker/Mindshare, Omnicom — OMD/PHD, Publicis — Starcom/Zenith, Dentsu — Carat/Isobar, IPG — Initiative/UM) provide scale, publisher relationships and integrated TV+digital planning.
- For programmatic, data-driven CTV and performance campaigns: specialist shops and programmatic partners (e.g., Simulmedia, Cadent, independent programmatic teams inside agencies, and DSP-driven agencies) often move faster on targeting, optimization and measurement.
- For scalable platform buys or self-serve managed services: platform-managed teams (Roku OneView, Hulu, X platform managed services) can deliver direct access to premium inventory.
- For creative/ad tech and measurement: vendors like Innovid, Samba TV, iSpot/Comscore (for measurement) complement agency buys — look for agencies that partner with these tools or provide in-house creative/tech.

What matters most when choosing
- Clear alignment to your goal: brand awareness vs direct response vs attribution.
- Inventory access and platform relationships (Roku, Hulu, Vizio, publishers).
- Targeting capabilities (household, household+device, identity resolution, third-party or first-party data).
- Measurement and attribution (viewability, reach/frequency, incremental lift testing, pixel or server-side integration).
- Transparency and fees (bid level reporting, media fees, data fees).
- Creative capabilities for CTV (30–60s spots, dynamic creative, A/B creative testing).
- Case studies and references in your vertical and geography.
- Reporting cadence and integrations with your BI/DMP/analytics tools.

Examples of reputable agencies/partners (to investigate)
- Global holding-group media agencies: Wavemaker, Mindshare, MediaCom, OMD, PHD, Starcom, Zenith, Carat, Initiative, UM — good for scale and cross-channel orchestration.
- CTV/TV-specialist firms: Simulmedia (data-driven linear + CTV), Cadent (addressable/CTV), Amobee (omnichannel programmatic), Tremor/SpotX/Magnite-adjacent teams — look for up-to-date capabilities in programmatic CTV.
- Platform managed services: Roku OneView, Hulu/Disney ad sales managed buys, Amazon/Twitch managed solutions — useful for premium inventory and integrated measurement.
- Creative & measurement partners: Innovid (dynamic creative & measurement), Samba TV / iSpot / Comscore (TV/CTV attribution and analytics).

Quick evaluation checklist / RFP starters
- What CTV platforms and publishers do you have direct relationships with?
- What targeting signals do you use (household, device, IP, deterministic IDs, second/third‑party data)?
- How do you measure incremental reach and lift? Can you run holdout/experimental tests?
- What reporting will we get (impression-level, bid-level, viewability, completion)?
- What are your media fees, data fees and technology fees?
- Can you produce or adapt creative for CTV (including dynamic creative)? Examples/case studies?
- Do you have references in our vertical and market (US/EU/APAC)?

If you tell me:
- your goal (brand vs performance),
- annual CTV budget,
- region(s),
- vertical (e.g., CPG, auto, direct-to-consumer, finance),
I can recommend 3–5 agencies or partners best suited to you and suggest an RFP template.
